text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- It was right for Denmark to give the United States permission to deploy nuclear weaponry in Greenland at the height of the Cold War between 1957 and 1968, prime minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen said. A commission report recently revealed that former prime ministers had kept Danes in the dark about Copenhagen's secret collusion with Washington over locating nuclear bombs on the icebound territory in defiance of Denmark's stated ban against such weaponry on Danish soil.
--- The permitted blood alcohol level for Danish car drivers is to be lowered from 0.8 percent to 0.5 percent, transport minister Bjoern Westh announced.
--- Danish companies have won orders worth some two billion crowns for improving the environment in eastern Europe over the next five years.

--- Due to economic problems, Danish dairy group MD Foods is to look into the possibility of merging with one or several British dairy groups in an effort to improve its results in the competitive U.K. market.
--- Only 20 percent of Nordic companies are prepared for the introduction of the European Union's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999, a survey shows.
